source_caption:
One of the most beloved and endearing moments in Good Will Hunting occurs in Sean Maguire’s office, when the therapist tells Will a deeply personal story about his late wife passing gas in her sleep and waking herself up. This entire wildly funny monologue was completely improvised by Robin Williams on the spot. Because the story was unscripted, Matt Damon had no idea what Williams was about to say, making his hysterical, breathless laughter entirely genuine. The ad-lib was so spontaneous and hilarious that it didn’t just break Damon; if you watch the final cut of the film closely during that scene, the camera itself visibly shakes up and down because the cameraman was laughing too hard to hold the shot completely steady.

Good Will Hunting (1997), directed by Gus Van Sant, starring Matt Damon, Robin Williams, Ben Affleck, Minnie Driver. A brilliant but rebellious, working-class math genius working as a janitor at MIT is forced to see a therapist who helps him confront his past and realize his full potential.

source_details.synopsis: Good Will Hunting is a 1997 American drama film directed by Gus Van Sant and written by Ben Affleck and Matt Damon. It stars Damon, Affleck, Robin Williams, Stellan Skarsgård, and Minnie Driver, with Casey Affleck and Cole Hauser in supporting roles. Set in Boston, the film follows Will Hunting (Damon), a troubled but self-taught genius working as a janitor at MIT, whose talent is discovered by professor Gerald Lambeau (Skarsgård). To avoid jail, Will agrees to study under Lambeau while attending therapy with psychologist Sean Maguire (Williams), which forces him to confront his past and his relationships, including with Harvard student Skylar (Driver).
